what_to_find: Confirm the ADU rules introduced in Scott County Zoning Ordinance No. 3 Comprehensive Revision #1, the revision’s exact adoption/effective dates, and separately identify changes in the Chapter 7 amendment effective 2025-05-06.
answer:
Scott County’s official Zoning Ordinance No. 3 cover confirms Comprehensive Revision #1 was adopted 2010-01-12 and effective 2010-01-20. County’s 2025 hearing materials state ADU regulations were adopted in the 2010 update after research/workshops, so ADUs were new in that revision (earlier code had separate temporary/family mobile-home provisions, not this ADU use). The 2023 pre-amendment code copy shows attached ADUs as administrative and detached as interim uses in applicable agricultural/residential districts; §7-4 standards included owner occupancy, family/caregiver occupant limit, one ADU, detached minimum 5 acres, 300-sf minimum and 40%/800-sf cap, room-count limits, 2 extra spaces, shared driveway and detached side/rear location 10–150 ft from the principal. Current Chapter 7 was amended effective 2025-05-06; this later rule is tracked separately. County controls only unincorporated township land; incorporated city parcels use city zoning. Exact ordinance number for the 2010 comprehensive revision is not stated on the cover.

2025 amendment comparison: Separate reform row for the Chapter 7 amendment effective 2025-05-06 (date stated in current official County ordinance amendment index). Compare official current Ordinance No.3 §7-4 with the 2023 pre-amendment copy: max size changed from a universal 40%/800-sf ceiling (and 300-sf minimum) to attached max 1,000 sf and detached max 1,200 sf; fixed 40% cap and 300-sf minimum removed; express IUP exception for maximum size of an existing structure added; old one-bath/one-kitchen/two-bedroom/one-utility-room ceiling removed; and the explicit side-or-rear-yard location clause removed. These are material relaxations. Still required: owner occupancy, family/caregiver occupancy, 5-acre minimum for detached ADU, one ADU per lot, two additional off-street spaces/shared driveway, 10–150-ft separation from principal structure, and no separate ownership. Attached remains administrative; detached remains interim in agricultural/residential districts per County hearing page. County code establishes effective date only; adoption ordinance number/date unresolved. County jurisdiction only in unincorporated township areas.

Second-coder status: 2010 adoption/effective dates confirmed; 2025 effective date confirmed; exact 2025 adoption date/ordinance number unresolved.

what_to_find: Verify Ramsey Ordinance 22-04 adoption/publication/effective dates, whether it first allowed ADUs, and principal standards.
answer:
CONFIRMED: Ramsey Ordinance 22-04 is the ADU ordinance. The ordinance text identifies it as an amendment to Chapter 117 (zoning), specifically §§117-1, 117-111, and 117-349, with an official summary saying it creates ADU requirements. It was adopted 2022-02-08, published 2022-02-11, and effective 2022-03-14 (30 days after passage and publication). The previously coded March 14 date is the effective date.

Novelty: Strong evidence this was the first general ADU authorization: §117-111 adds ADUs to permitted uses, defines CUP permission for conversion of a lawful nonconforming garage, and §117-349 replaces “Reserved” with ADU standards. Ordinance summary says it creates ADU requirements. No earlier general ADU allowance found in this search; a comprehensive pre-2022 ordinance-by-ordinance audit was not available.

Basic rule in Ord.22-04: R-1 district; attached and detached ADUs permitted by right subject to standards; no more than one per existing single-family property; principal dwelling or ADU must be owner-occupied; 800 sf max habitable area; detached minimum lot size one acre; attached minimum lot width 80 feet; height max 22 feet or principal-structure height, whichever less; R-1 dwelling setbacks; no added parking if principal structure’s off-street parking requirements are met; shared utilities; permanent foundation, building permit and Certificate of Occupancy; no separate sale/tax parcel; CUP only for converting lawful nonconforming garage.

Source: Ordinance 22-04 PDF, pp.1-3 (especially p.3 dates and effective-date section): https://mcclibraryfunctions.azurewebsites.us/api/ordinanceDownload/14286/1135523/pdf; City 2023 zoning packet, p.50, reproduces standards for later code update: https://public.destinyhosted.com/ramsedocs/2023/PlanReg/20230427_23153/AGENDApacket__04-27-23_1054_23152.pdf.

what_to_find: Confirm Ordinance 811 adoption and separate effective/publication dates; extract current Chapter 937 ADU districts and standards.
answer:
Confirmed as Ordinance 811. The June 21, 2022 City Council packet contains the ordinance text and its adoption clause; the official meeting summary lists the second reading/adoption as consent item 7.h and says the consent agenda passed 4-0. The adopted code packet states: “This Ordinance will become effective upon passage and publication” and is adopted June 21, 2022. The publication line on the ordinance page is blank. The city code history for Chapter 937 carries “Ord. 811 [6-30-2022]”; this supports June 30, 2022 as the codification/effective date but is not a proof-of-publication record. Record adoption as 2022-06-21; effective date as 2022-06-30 (code-history date, publication linkage not independently confirmed); exact publication record remains Unresolved.

The city’s zoning-study page says Ordinance 811 introduced ADUs as a permitted-with-conditions use in all single-family zoning districts (R-1A, R-1, R-2A, R-2, R-3A, R-3). Table 937.02 marks them A/P (permitted accessory use); not a CUP in those districts. Chapter 937.03(A): minimum 300 sq. ft.; max 33% of principal home gross habitable space; additional 960-sq.-ft. cap only in R-2A, R-2, R-3A and R-3. Detached ADUs allowed; in R-3A/R-3, detached units require at least 11,000-sq.-ft. lots. One off-street space dedicated to ADU plus two for primary residence; either principal home or ADU must be owner-occupied; rental license required if renter-occupied; max one ADU per lot. New detached ADUs follow principal-structure setbacks; pre-June 30, 2022 accessory structures converted to ADUs may use accessory-structure setbacks.

Adoption: 2022-06-21, Ord. 811; effective: 2022-06-30 per code history, not independently tied to publication; publication: Unresolved. Second-coder status: confirmed, publication evidence gap.

what_to_find: Confirm Ordinance number/adoption, publication/effective dates, pre-2025 ADU status, and current §1306.030 standards.
answer: CONFIRMED: White Bear Lake adopted Ordinance No. 25-07-2080 on 2025-07-22 (Council minutes, unanimous). Council Resolution No. 13536 approved title/summary publication on that date. White Bear Press published the summary on 2025-08-20; the official adopted code expressly states effective 2025-08-20 (§1301.010.3). The 2025 change did NOT introduce ADUs: former §1302.125 allowed permanent “home accessory apartments” in residential districts where single-family homes were permitted, by conditional use permit; owner had to live in the principal home. The source history cites Ord.02-08-993 (8/13/02) and Ord.16-10-2019 (10/11/16). Current §1306.030 allows max one ADU/lot inside the principal home, by addition, or in a detached accessory building. It is allowed with Lakefront House or Detached House building types: Table 1302-2 means lakefront house in R-1/R-2a/R-2b/R-2c and detached house in R-3/R-4/R-5. City describes ADUs as “allowed by right”; administrative/zoning/building reviews still apply. ADU size: min 200 sf for first occupant plus 100 sf each additional; max lesser of 880 sf or 50% of principal dwelling floor area. Combined household occupancy cap is one household plus two additional adults. Owner with ≥50% interest must occupy either dwelling unit as permanent home for most calendar days; affidavit/deed restriction before permit. No additional parking required if principal home off-street parking remains. Utilities connect to principal building; no separate driveway/curb cut; sewer adequacy evaluation and building/life-safety plan review. No standalone numeric lot minimum specific to the ADU; underlying building type, lot, accessory-structure, setback and shoreland standards continue to apply. ADU is an accessory use and must not be confused with duplex/multi-unit principal building types.

what_to_find: What Rochester's pre-2023 code allowed for 2-4 units in R-1 and other districts.
answer: Historical answer (old LDM, before UDC effective 2023-01-01): permissions were district-specific. The strongest official record located is the City's 1998 staff report and Planning Commission minutes: after an amendment, R-1 (Mixed Single Family) no longer allowed duplexes or Performance Residential Developments (PRDs); R-1x (Mixed Single Family Extra) retained the former R-1 use set, including PRDs, subject to its performance standards. The record describes duplexes as an allowed use in R-1 before that amendment. It also treats townhomes/attached units through PRD standards, not as a blanket citywide entitlement. A 3- or 4-unit proposal was not automatically permitted on an ordinary R-1 lot; the 1998 file discusses a fourplex proposal requiring rezoning/approval and variances. Other districts (R-2 and higher-density districts) and parcel-specific Planned Unit Developments/Special Districts had separate rules. I could not verify a complete final-2022 district use table for duplex/triplex/fourplex from the archived official LDM in this pass, so the exact rules for every old district and whether 3–4 unit buildings were permitted/conditional in each remain unresolved. Distinguish these principal multi-unit buildings from ADUs. Official source excerpts: City staff says R-1 “was revised to remove Performance Residential Developments and Duplexes”; “R-1x is the old R-1 district”; and a Planning Commission member states duplexes could have been built in R-1 before the change. The UDC replaced Ordinance 2785 effective 2023-01-01.
